methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series C → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.7x) to $356M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Gatik is a Series C autonomous transportation company that has raised $355.6M to date. The relevant peer universe consists of eight private frontier-tech companies in the Transportation sector, including Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Slate Auto, and ZeroAvia. No public comparables exist in this narrow stage and subsector.

Given the absence of sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage peers meeting minimum density thresholds (fewer than three datapoints in filtered sets), peer-median valuation is not applicable. The Stage-Progression method is therefore the primary triangulation approach, applying a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C progression to the $356M raised proxy, yielding $605M.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $514M (low) to $695M (high), with a median estimate of $605M. This range reflects primarily the Stage-Progression methodology and carries corresponding uncertainty around the appropriateness of the 1.7x multiplier for this particular company and market moment. Key uncertainties include the scarcity of direct peer benchmarks at Gatik's stage and the inherent variability in step-up multiples across frontier transportation ventures. Additional comparable transaction data or company-specific unit economics would materially strengthen conviction in this range.
